runs.content: Tuesday's rotation focus is AI & Tech + Technology. Since the last thinker run (2026-09-14, Monday), log.md's top-of-file section showed only two routine Finance tracker updates (sector-performance-tracker, book-recommender) — but a deeper check of file modification times turned up a substantial, unlogged-at-top evening session on 2026-09-14: a clippings-sorter run processed 7 clippings, including two new Michael Burry trading posts, four Citrini 'Global Macro Trading for Idiots' pages, and one AI & Tech clipping — Kakashii's skeptical line-by-line annotation of the April 2026 Dwarkesh x Jensen Huang interview. That single new AI & Tech page turned up two genuinely new findings. Investigation idea: Kakashii's point 4 argues the GPU shortage ended in late 2024 and Nvidia has been in an oversupply regime since (GPUs sitting unassigned in warehouses) — a live, present-tense dispute against the dominant supply-constrained narrative built up across ai-tech/data-hbm-supply-chain-2026-06-27.md ('sold out through 2026-2027') and ai-tech/model-ai-ecosystem-constraint-edges-2026-06-27.md (CoWoS/TSMC as binding chokepoint), both of which only model oversupply as a theoretical 2027+ bear case, not something already happening at the GPU level today. Cross-domain connection: the Kakashii page explicitly states its neocloud-demand-engineering argument is 'structurally the same argument Burry makes about off-balance-sheet AI financing' and links twice to finance/michael-burry/index.md — but that Finance hub page, updated in the very same ingestion session with two new trading posts and an active NVDA short, has no reverse link back (a grep for 'kakashii' in the file returns nothing), unlike the Kakashii page's other cross-link (to the neutral Dwarkesh-Jensen episode notes), which the same run did make bidirectional. Checked the open sections for resolution: nothing showed clear signs of being actioned since 2026-09-14.

Monday's rotation focus is Finance + Crypto. Since the last thinker run (2026-09-13, Sunday), log.md shows only two mechanical Finance tracker refreshes (sector-performance-tracker, growth-value-tracker) plus a Strategy Feedback review and the routine end-of-day memory update — no new source material was clipped or ingested, an unusually quiet window. Deep-read Finance's newest model page, finance/models/model-hyperscaler-debt-capex-rate-exposure-2026-09-10.md (built 2026-09-10, SEC EDGAR debt/capex/rate-exposure ranking across MSFT/AMZN/GOOGL/META/ORCL/CRWV/PLTR), and Crypto's core pages (crypto-overview, crypto-portfolio, defi-watchlist) in full. One genuinely new, non-duplicate investigation idea cleared the bar: the model page's own Data Source Note describes the tool that produced it — `carry-trade-debt-monitor`, a self-hosted SEC EDGAR XBRL scraper with a live dashboard (localhost:8420) that has now underpinned two separate Finance models — as 'not yet published to the wiki as its own project.' A grep of wiki/ai-tech/ confirms it: ai-tech/projects.md, the domain's own 'All software/app/AI projects' index, still lists exactly one entry (Crypto App) plus an empty placeholder row, unchanged since 2026-05-01. This is the identical pattern the wiki-thinker already caught and closed for Lightfin's AI-video pipeline on 2026-07-17 — a real, actively-used AI build invisible from the one page meant to catalog it — just recurring for a different tool. Crypto's own pages (overview, portfolio, defi-watchlist) were read in full but turned up nothing new: the one live cross-domain thread there (SmarDex's USDN stablecoin vs. the Bessent Treasury-reserve stablecoin thesis) is already cross-linked in defi-watchlist.md's own See Also. No new cross-domain connection cleared the bar today. Checked the open sections for resolution: nothing showed clear signs of being actioned since 2026-09-13.
